ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, and C are all on $\odot O$. If $\angle AOC = \angle ABC$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle A + \angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\paragraph{Solution:} Let's look at the diagram: Select a point $D$ on the major arc $AC$, and connect $AD$ and $CD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC$, $\angle ADC+\angle ABC=180^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle AOC=\angle ABC$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC+\angle ABC=180^\circ$, which yields: $\angle ABC=120^\circ$\\
$\because$ in quadrilateral $ABCD$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A+\angle C+\angle ABC+\angle AOC=360^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A+\angle C=360^\circ-2\angle ABC=\boxed{120^\circ}$.

Thus x = 1/2(360° - x), giving x = 120°. Then use the angle sum of quadrilateral A-B-C-O: ∠A + ∠ABC + ∠C + ∠AOC = 360°.
